new_entities.name: Craniosacral therapy
new_entities.description: A manual therapy approach based on gentle palpation and manipulation of the skull, spine, and surrounding tissues.

edges.effect_quant: A 2019 meta-analysis pooled 10 randomized trials involving 681 patients and reported significant effects on pain and function, but earlier reviews emphasized that the underlying study base was sparse and methodologically weak, making broad clinical claims unreliable.
edges.population: adults with chronic pain or other symptoms treated with craniosacral therapy in clinical trials
edges.mechanism: Gentle manual contact may alter relaxation, expectancy, and nonspecific symptom appraisal, but the core craniosacral premises remain weakly validated and outcome evidence is inconsistent across conditions.
edges.summary: This is best handled as a contested manual-therapy claim rather than a robust evidence-based treatment edge. Some trials report symptom improvements, especially in pain-focused settings, but the broader craniosacral evidence base remains small, heterogeneous, and vulnerable to bias.
edges.caveats: Do not overgeneralize pain-trial findings into proof of broad systemic benefit. The positive signal is mostly patient-reported and does not validate the underlying craniosacral explanatory model.
